In actions_summary.txt, the file must reference the chargeback (SafeGuard/VSC/$2,800), the funding delay (Wells Fargo/SL-2026-0412), the trade payoff variance ($290), the cash discrepancy ($180), and the floorplan sold-not-paid status.
In mailbox.json, a sent email must be addressed to elena.brooks@sunshineauto.com and reference the chargeback and deal SL-2026-0412.

In mailbox.json or slack.json, one sent email addressed to both noah.alvarez@sunshineauto.com and elena.brooks@sunshineauto.com, or one assistant Slack message that names or directly includes both, must contain the Wells Fargo funding escalation fields required by the SOP: deal SL-2026-0412, the EOD April 14, 2026 deadline, the original notarized Power of Attorney, and the payoff letter showing an account number and good-through date.

In mailbox.json, one sent trade payoff email addressed to both priya.bennett@sunshineauto.com and elena.brooks@sunshineauto.com must contain the SOP-required numeric fields: $290 payoff variance, $5,000 original total gross, $2,910 recalculated front gross, $4,710 recalculated total gross, and the $51-$500 tier. General prose quality and semantic label binding are not graded by this criterion.

In mailbox.json or slack.json, darius.kim@sunshineauto.com and elena.brooks@sunshineauto.com must each receive a sent email or an assistant Slack message that names or directly includes them and references the sold-not-paid status, VIN 8XJ472, or floorplan interest accrual.
In mailbox.json, no sent escalation email may have marcus.hale@sunshineauto.com as the sole internal recipient without elena.brooks@sunshineauto.com also addressed.

In actions_summary.txt, the file must reference Elena Brooks (Controller) in connection with the cash discrepancy and must also reference Noah Alvarez, Priya Bennett, Renee Lawson, and Darius Kim; each person may be identified by full name, unique first name or surname, unique role title, or email handle.
verifier_code:
from pathlib import Path
import re

# Identifier patterns: full name (dotted or spaced), unique first name, unique
# surname, unique role title, or email handle (the dotted-name alternative also
# matches the local part of the person's email address). Roles/names are unique
# in this task's SOP team directory. "Assistant Controller" is Marcus Hale, so
# a bare "controller" preceded by assistant/asst does NOT identify Elena.
ELENA_PAT = r'elena.?brooks|elena\.brooks|\belena\b|\bbrooks\b|(?<!assistant )(?<!asst\. )(?<!asst )\bcontroller\b'
NOAH_PAT = r'noah.?alvarez|noah\.alvarez|\bnoah\b|\balvarez\b|funding\s*(?:&|and)\s*contracts\s+clerk|funding\s+clerk'
PRIYA_PAT = r'priya.?bennett|priya\.bennett|\bpriya\b|\bbennett\b|titles\s*(?:&|and)\s*billing\s+clerk|titles\s+clerk|billing\s+clerk'
RENEE_PAT = r'renee.?lawson|renee\.lawson|\brenee\b|\blawson\b|\bcashier\b|receivables\s+clerk'
DARIUS_PAT = r'darius.?kim|darius\.kim|\bdarius\b|\bkim\b|inventory\s+accountant'
CASH_PAT = r'cash|deposit|discrepancy|\$180|180|shortage'

def verify(workspace_path, external_services_path=None):
    actions_file = Path(workspace_path) / 'actions_summary.txt'
    if not actions_file.exists():
        return {'pass': False, 'score': 0.0, 'feedback': 'actions_summary.txt not found in workspace'}
    content = actions_file.read_text(encoding='utf-8', errors='ignore').lower()
    required_people = [
        ('elena.brooks or elena brooks', bool(re.search(ELENA_PAT, content))),
        ('noah.alvarez or noah alvarez', bool(re.search(NOAH_PAT, content))),
        ('priya.bennett or priya bennett', bool(re.search(PRIYA_PAT, content))),
        ('renee.lawson or renee lawson', bool(re.search(RENEE_PAT, content))),
        ('darius.kim or darius kim', bool(re.search(DARIUS_PAT, content))),
    ]
    missing = [name for name, found in required_people if not found]
    found = [name for name, found in required_people if found]
    # Additionally check that Elena Brooks is referenced in the context of cash discrepancy.
    # The proximity window spans line breaks (re.DOTALL); as a fallback, any
    # blank-line-delimited section mentioning both Elena and a cash keyword counts.
    elena_cash_context = bool(re.search(
        r'(?:' + CASH_PAT + r').{0,200}(?:' + ELENA_PAT + r')|(?:' + ELENA_PAT + r').{0,200}(?:' + CASH_PAT + r')',
        content, re.DOTALL))
    if not elena_cash_context:
        for section in re.split(r'\n\s*\n', content):
            if re.search(ELENA_PAT, section) and re.search(CASH_PAT, section):
                elena_cash_context = True
                break
    if missing:
        return {'pass': False, 'score': len(found) / len(required_people), 'feedback': f'actions_summary.txt missing references to: {missing}. Found: {found}'}
    if not elena_cash_context:
        return {'pass': False, 'score': 0.8, 'feedback': f'actions_summary.txt references all recipients but does not associate elena.brooks with the cash discrepancy (month-end close threshold override). Found all names: {[name for name, _ in required_people]}'}
    return {'pass': True, 'score': 1.0, 'feedback': f'actions_summary.txt references all required recipients including elena.brooks for cash discrepancy: {[name for name, _ in required_people]}'}

rubric_text: In actions_summary.txt, the file must not reference marcus.hale as the primary escalation handler and must reference elena.brooks as the backup or replacement for marcus.hale.

In mailbox.json, the sent trade payoff email addressed to priya.bennett@sunshineauto.com and elena.brooks@sunshineauto.com must include the figures `$5,000` for the original total gross, `$4,710` for the recalculated total gross, and `$51–$500` tier classification.

In actions_summary.txt, the section about trade payoff variance must state `$5,000` for the original total gross, `$4,710` for the recalculated total gross, classify the $290 gross adjustment under the `$51–$500` tier, and must escalate the issue to Elena Brooks without a 1 business day (or 1 BD) delay.
verifier_code:
from pathlib import Path
import re

def verify(workspace_path, external_services_path=None):
    actions_file = Path(workspace_path) / 'actions_summary.txt'
    if not actions_file.exists():
        return {'pass': False, 'score': 0.0,
                'feedback': 'actions_summary.txt not found in workspace.'}

    raw = actions_file.read_text(encoding='utf-8', errors='ignore')
    text = raw.lower()

    checks = {}

    # 1. Original total gross of $5,000 (allow $5,000 or $5000)
    checks['original_gross_5000'] = bool(
        re.search(r'\$\s*5[,\s]?000(?!\d)', text)
    )

    # 2. Recalculated total gross of $4,710 (allow $4,710 or $4710)
    checks['recalculated_gross_4710'] = bool(
        re.search(r'\$\s*4[,\s]?710(?!\d)', text)
    )

    # 3. $290 adjustment classified under the $51–$500 tier.
    #    Accept the amount with or without a dollar sign, and treat the
    #    amount and the tier as linked when they appear in the same
    #    blank-line-delimited paragraph or within 800 characters, so a
    #    payoff section stating both facts is not rejected for spacing.
    tier_pattern = r'(?<!\d)\$?\s*51\s*(?:[-–—]+|to|through|and)\s*\$?\s*500'
    amount_pattern = r'(?<![\d,.])\$?\s*290(?:\.00)?\b(?!\.\d)(?!,\d)'
    adj_290 = [m.start() for m in re.finditer(amount_pattern, text)]
    tier_hits = [m.start() for m in re.finditer(tier_pattern, text)]
    paragraph_spans = []
    para_start = 0
    for blank in re.finditer(r'\n\s*\n', text):
        paragraph_spans.append((para_start, blank.start()))
        para_start = blank.end()
    paragraph_spans.append((para_start, len(text)))

    def same_paragraph(a, t):
        return any(s <= a < e and s <= t < e for s, e in paragraph_spans)

    near = False
    for a in adj_290:
        for t in tier_hits:
            if abs(a - t) <= 800 or same_paragraph(a, t):
                near = True
                break
        if near:
            break
    checks['290_in_51_500_tier'] = near

    # 4. Escalation to Elena Brooks
    checks['escalated_to_elena_brooks'] = bool(
        re.search(r'elena\s+brooks', text)
    )

    # 5. No 1 business day / 1 BD delay before the Elena Brooks escalation.
    #    Only fail on statements that the agent waited or will wait
    #    ("wait 1 business day", "1 BD delay", "will escalate ... after
    #    1 business day").  Accurate documentation of the SOP 2.4 SLA
    #    ("Marcus Hale must respond within 1 business day ...") and
    #    negated phrasings ("without a 1 business day delay", "rather
    #    than waiting 1 business day") must not fail this check.
    one_bd = r'\b(?:1|one)[\s-]*(?:bd\b|business[\s-]*day)'
    future = r'(?:will|shall|going\s+to|plan(?:ning|s)?\s+to|intend(?:s|ing)?\s+to)'
    no_neg_words = r'(?:(?!not\b|no\b|never\b)\w+[\s,]+){0,6}?'
    gap = r'(?:(?!rather\s+than|instead\s+of)[^.\n;:]){0,80}?'
    wait_patterns = [
        r'(?:wait(?:ing|ed|s)?|held|hold(?:ing)?(?:\s+off)?|delay(?:ing|ed|s)?|'
        r'defer(?:ring|red|s)?|postpon(?:e|es|ed|ing))\s+' + no_neg_words + one_bd,
        one_bd + r'[\s-]+(?:delay|wait|hold)',
        future + r'\s+' + no_neg_words + r'escalat\w*' + gap +
        r'(?:after|following|once|in|within)\s+' + one_bd,
        r'(?:after|following|once|in|within)\s+' + one_bd + gap +
        future + r'\s+' + no_neg_words + r'escalat\w*',
    ]
    negations = (
        r"(?:\b(?:without|not|never|avoid(?:s|ing|ed)?|rather\s+than|"
        r"instead\s+of|skip(?:s|ping|ped)?|bypass(?:es|ing|ed)?|"
        r"eliminat(?:e|es|ing|ed)|remov(?:e|es|ing|ed)|won[’']t|"
        r"will\s+not|did\s+not|didn[’']t|do(?:es)?\s+not|doesn[’']t)"
        r"\s+(?:\w+\s+){0,4}|\bno\s+)$"
    )
    has_bad_delay = False
    for pat in wait_patterns:
        for m in re.finditer(pat, text):
            prefix = text[max(0, m.start() - 60):m.start()]
            if re.search(negations, prefix):
                continue
            has_bad_delay = True
            break
        if has_bad_delay:
            break
    checks['no_1bd_delay'] = not has_bad_delay

    passed = [k for k, v in checks.items() if v]
    missing = [k for k, v in checks.items() if not v]

    if not missing:
        return {'pass': True, 'score': 1.0,
                'feedback': f'All checks passed: {passed}'}
    return {'pass': False, 'score': len(passed) / len(checks),
            'feedback': f'Passed: {passed}; Failed: {missing}'}
